text.p: Merck and Co Inc on Wednesday said it was comfortable with Wall Street analysts' estimates for its fourth quarter earnings in a range of $0.80 to $0.86 a share, but implied the bottom end of the range was too low.
"We're comfortable within that range," Merck director of investor relations Jim Hinrichs told analysts in a conference call after the company's third quarter earnings report.

"But when you have a number at the bottom of that range, it's not really consistent with the guidance we've been giving all year of stronger earnings in the second half relative to the first half," he said.

Hinrichs said that adding the range of fourth quarter estimates to the company's earnings of $2.33 a share for the first nine months of the year, Merck backed estimates for its full-year earnings in a $3.13-to-$3.19 range.
First Call listed the mean Wall Street estimate for Merck's 1996 earnings at $3.13 a share, with a range of 27 estimates between $3.10 and $3.19. The drug giant reported earnings of $2.70 a year ago.
Earlier this year the company had said it was comfortable with 1996 estimates in a $3.00-to-$3.15 range.
Merck on Wednesday posted third quarter earnings per share of $0.83, up from $0.70 a year ago, beating the First Call consensus of $0.81.
